content.text:
Confirmed. The bridge's embedded Tailscale node (`cmux-bridge-mini`) has **never been logged in** — it's stuck in `NeedsLogin`, looping on `up failed` and printing the same login URL. It is **not on your tailnet**.

Here's the mechanism: `cmux-bridge --pair --tailscale` calls `startTailscaleForPairing`, which spins up the bridge's own `tsnet` node and waits (60s) for it to come up so it can read back the `.ts.net` hostname. Because that node was never authenticated, `tsnet.Up` fails, the function returns an **empty** host, and `PrintQR` then falls back to the LAN-only QR (and even prints the misleading "re-run `--pair --tailscale`" hint — which you already did).

So `--tailscale` *was* honored; it just had nothing to embed because the node isn't authenticated. That auth is the one-time interactive step I flagged earlier that hasn't been completed.

## Fix — authenticate the bridge's Tailscale node (one time)

1. On any browser signed into your tailnet (`tail901772.ts.net`, owner `moltopenclawbot@`), open the login URL the daemon is currently offering:

   **https://login.tailscale.com/a/b51d8b501c3c6**

   Approve the node when prompted — it'll register as `cmux-bridge-mini`. (The daemon is running and holding this session open, so approving it will let `tsnet.Up` finally succeed and persist credentials.)

2. Verify it came up:
   ```bash
   # on the mini
   grep "tailscale: listening on" ~/Library/Logs/cmux-bridge.log | tail -1
   ```
   You want a line like `tailscale: listening on cmux-bridge-mini.tail901772.ts.net:47821`.

3. Re-run pairing — now the QR will include the tailnet host:
   ```bash
   cmux-bridge --pair --tailscale
   ```

If that login URL has gone stale (approve fails), restart the daemon to mint a fresh one: `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.itsmaleen.cmux-bridge`, then re-grep the log for the new `login.tailscale.com/...` line.

## There's also a real UX bug here worth fixing
`--pair --tailscale` **silently degraded to a LAN-only QR** instead of telling you "Tailscale isn't authenticated — visit this URL." That's exactly why this was confusing. I'd like to fix the bridge so that when `--tailscale` is requested but the node can't come up, it **surfaces the login URL and refuses to emit a LAN-only QR** (or at least warns loudly that the flag was dropped).

Want me to make that fix (its own small PR against the bridge)? And once you've approved the login URL, I can verify end-to-end that `cmux-bridge-mini` is on the tailnet and the next pairing embeds the host.

gh pr create --base main --title "fix(bridge): don't emit a LAN-only QR when --pair --tailscale can't come up" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

Running \`cmux-bridge --pair --tailscale\` could print a **LAN-only** QR even though \`--tailscale\` was passed. The phone then paired "successfully" but sat on **reconnecting** whenever it was off the home Wi-Fi.

Root cause: if the bridge's embedded tsnet node wasn't authenticated yet, \`startTailscaleForPairing\` blocked until a 60s timeout, returned an empty host, and \`PrintQR\` silently fell back to a QR with no \`tailscale_host\`. The one hint it printed ("re-run \`--pair --tailscale\`") was misleading because the user *had* passed the flag — the real blocker was an un-authorized Tailscale node.

## Fix

- **Surface the login URL.** tsnet emits the interactive auth URL through its \`Logf\`; we now parse it out and print a clear "Tailscale login required — open this URL and approve `<hostname>`" message, then wait up to **3 minutes** for authorization (was a silent 60s).
- **Never silently degrade.** If the node still doesn't come up, \`--pair\` now **fails loudly** with actionable guidance (authorize the node; and if the background daemon is running, stop it first since it holds the tsnet state dir) instead of emitting a LAN-only QR.

Behavior when the node is already authorized is unchanged: \`ts.Up\` returns immediately and the QR includes the tailnet host.

## Testing
- \`go build ./...\`, \`go vet ./cmd/cmux-bridge/\` clean.
- Reproduced the original silent-LAN degradation against an unauthorized node; with the change the login URL is surfaced and, if unauthorized, pairing exits non-zero with guidance rather than printing a LAN QR.

Context: this is the confusing behavior that made a freshly-paired Mac mini show remote access in the QR only after the node was manually authorized out-of-band.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3
